# Index

10 cases, newest first. Each line: the case's label (the name the lessons and the checklist use for it), title — case type (product, benchmark or study): the interface or set of interfaces; what AI did; what was measured; what the AI's output was checked against (people, an automated checker, a model judge); the sample; how far the claims can be checked; the author's stake in the tools (maintainer-own marks the maintainer's own project); the cost the source gives; a one-line summary.

Lessons drawn from the cases, by aspect: [lessons/index.md](lessons/index.md) (49 lessons on 5 pages). To measure a project: [checklist.md](checklist.md).

Cases covered: By type: product 3, benchmark 2, study 5. What AI did: design 2, build 4, change 4, check 8, judge 3, simulate-user 2. Checked against: people 5, checker 3, model 3, none 1 (a case may count under several).

- **studio-go**: [studio-go's video UI passes every agent-written rule test yet stays costly to use; a newcomer agent and a job walk count it](cases/2026-11-14-studio-go-interface-redesign.md) — product: the local web UI of a single-owner video pipeline, its pages after a first round of fixes and the clickable mocks of a redesign; AI: design, build, change, check, simulate-user; measured: task-cost, function, consistency, contrast, human-preference, cost; checked against: checker, model; sample: 1 web app with 1 user (its owner), 6 jobs, 40 audit findings, 6 mockups (65 HTML pages at one count, 32 HTML pages later); evidence: assertion-only; author: maintainer-own; cost: wall time only, between 14 minutes and roughly 2.5 hours per package for the 12 packages after the job walk; tokens and money not recorded for this work. Agents landed 39 of 40 UI packages (20 of 40 findings complete) with rule tests green, yet jobs stayed long; a newcomer agent and a job walk counted them.
- **Agentic audit**: [One browser agent per WCAG criterion finds more audit-reported barriers than axe-core or a single-pass model, and more unlisted ones](cases/2026-09-08-mishra-agentic-a11y-audit.md) — benchmark: saved copies of 24 pages from eleven scholarly publishing platforms, audited against 40 WCAG success criteria; AI: check; measured: accessibility, issue-coverage, cost; checked against: people; sample: 250 page-criterion pairs (78 reported failures, 172 pairs inferred to pass) on 24 pages; 40 criteria, 15 criteria with a reported failure; 9 compared runs in the main table, 4 later worker runs, 6 further batch model runs; evidence: shown-in-source; author: independent; cost: USD 6.38 to USD 74.52 per 250-pair workload, estimates (API-equivalent for the coding agents); the reference worker run has no usage record. Per-criterion agents found 67 of 78 barriers in expert audits (axe-core 28) at 56% precision; their lead was largest on keyboard failures.
- **Concordia repair**: [Kimi K2.5 repairs 308 scraped pages; most improve, a quarter pass axe, and a retry loop adds cost but no fixes](cases/2026-05-26-concordia-llm-accessibility-repair.md) — study: static HTML of scraped real-world web pages (news, education, standards sites), checked for accessibility violations and then repaired; AI: check, change; measured: accessibility, issue-coverage, cost; checked against: checker; sample: 662 pages for detection (331 pages with violations, 331 corrected pages); 308 pages repaired by each of two strategies; 1 model, 1 run reported; evidence: shown-in-source; author: independent; cost: $4.92 for the single-pass repair of 308 pages and $7.50 for the agent loop, as reported; the code prices tokens at fixed GPT-4o-mini rates. Kimi K2.5 cut axe violations from 3.98 violations to 1.7 violations per page; a quarter of 308 pages came out clean; a retry loop cost 52% more, fixed no more.
- **GitHub a11y agent**: [GitHub's accessibility agent reviews front-end pull requests with one reviewer and one fixer, and is told to refuse risky patterns](cases/2026-05-15-github-accessibility-agent.md) — product: pull requests that change GitHub's front-end code, reviewed for WCAG issues by an agent that also answers accessibility questions in Copilot CLI and VS Code; AI: check, change; measured: accessibility; checked against: none; sample: 3,535 pull requests reviewed; evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. GitHub's pilot agent reviewed 3,535 pull requests at a 68% "resolution rate" it never defines; it hands complex code and risky widgets to people.
- **Anthropic harness**: [Anthropic adds a planner and a Playwright grading agent to Claude app builds; by the engineer's account the game maker works where a solo run broke, at over 20x the cost](cases/2026-03-24-anthropic-harness-design.md) — product: web front ends from a one-line prompt, then two full-stack browser apps (a retro game maker and a music workstation) built by Claude agents; AI: design, build, check, judge; measured: function, cost; checked against: model; sample: 2 full-stack apps built with the harness and 1 solo run for comparison; front-end runs of 5 to 15 iterations each, number of runs unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: game maker $9 solo against $200 with the harness; music workstation $124.70 in tokens. A Claude grader clicking through each sprint filed bugs and the game played where a solo run broke; the grader needed tuning, missed bugs, cost over 20x.
- **UW walkthrough**: [GPT-4 and Gemini walk two mobile apps more directly than people and flag fewer failure points until asked to rate confusion](cases/2025-12-03-uw-synthetic-cognitive-walkthrough.md) — study: two mobile apps, one for learning a language and one for booking trips, given to the models as screenshot sets, six tasks each; AI: simulate-user, judge; measured: task-cost, judge-agreement; checked against: people; sample: 10 participants; 16 LLM runs in study 1; 12 LLM runs in study 2 (3 per model per condition); 2 apps, 12 tasks; evidence: shown-in-source; author: independent; cost: unstated. LLM walkthroughs beat 10 people on app tasks yet raised 3 failure points to their 10; confusion ratings during the walk predicted where people doubted.
- **ArtifactsBench**: [ArtifactsBench has an LLM judge score generated web artifacts from screenshots and a checklist; the expert check covers a small subset](cases/2025-07-07-tencent-artifactsbench.md) — benchmark: self-contained web artifacts (games, SVG graphics, web apps, simulations, dashboards, management systems, small tools) generated by LLMs from one prompt each; AI: build, judge; measured: function, judge-agreement; checked against: people, model; sample: 1,825 queries; 33 models in the main table, 22 in the stable-judge table, 25 in the open-judge table; expert check on 280 queries from 6 models; 12 models compared with WebDev Arena; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. A Gemini judge scored answers to 1,825 web-artifact queries from screenshots and checklists; its 90.95% expert agreement rests on 280 queries from 6 models.
- **UW heuristic review**: [GPT-4 heuristic reviews of two mobile apps cover more issues than five pooled experts but miss half the cross-screen ones](cases/2025-07-03-uw-synthetic-heuristic-evaluation.md) — study: screenshots of two mobile apps, one for renting a flat and one for learning a language, four user tasks each, reviewed against Nielsen's 10 heuristics; AI: check; measured: issue-coverage, run-stability; checked against: people; sample: 2 apps, 8 tasks; 10 freelance UX experts (5 per app); five research assistants for the reference set; GPT-4 repeated on two accounts over 3 months; outputs from Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Gemini-1.5-pro (runs unstated); evidence: shown-in-source; author: independent; cost: unstated. GPT-4 covered 73% and 77% of known issues against 57% and 63% for five pooled UX experts, yet raised more non-issues and missed cross-screen problems.
- **Brazil heuristic review**: [GPT-4o reviews 20 screenshots of a mining-data website against Nielsen's heuristics and finds a fifth of the experts' issues](cases/2025-06-19-unespar-gpt4o-heuristic-evaluation.md) — study: a public Brazilian web platform of maps and charts on mineral research and production, given to the model as 20 screenshots and reviewed against Nielsen's 10 heuristics; AI: check; measured: issue-coverage; checked against: people; sample: 20 screenshots, one model run each; 66 issues from an earlier review by 3 experts; four researchers classified the model's issues; evidence: shown-in-source; author: independent; cost: unstated. From 20 screenshots GPT-4o raised 111 issues; 41 survived review, 14 of them among 66 expert issues (21.2%), and 27 were false positives.
- **UCI code study**: [Qwen2.5-Coder and GPT-4o rewrite ten real websites with lower checker violation rates than the original code, but not on ARIA](cases/2025-03-20-uci-human-or-llm-accessible-code.md) — study: UI files (HTML, JavaScript, CSS) of ten open-source project websites, regenerated block by block from model-written summaries and rendered; AI: build, check, change; measured: accessibility, contrast, function; checked against: checker; sample: 10 projects; 473 sampled UI files; 10 pages per project; 2 newer projects in a leakage check; 2 models; evidence: shown-in-source; author: independent; cost: unstated. Rewritten from summaries, model code had lower checker violation rates than human code; accessibility prompts rarely helped, a model-report fix loop mostly did.
